correctness.rationale: For each finite positive time and at stationarity, the Lyapunov equation integrates to a positive Laplace Gram kernel. The strict 2x2 total-positivity determinant obstructs every three-distinct-rate triple, while strict Cauchy--Schwarz obstructs every two-group 2+2 off-diagonal tetrad. Explicit singleton-factor construction proves sufficiency and uniqueness-zero diagonals on the allowed patterns. Four-entry perturbation bounds turn the positive defects into rigorous positive Frobenius lower bounds. Defects have positive order-t^4 coefficients, model entries have order t, and midpoint rank-one construction has O(t^3) error; hence the distance is Θ(t^3). Symbolic rational and series verification and a reproducible 4002-check standalone script corroborate specific computations; finite tests are not treated as universal proof.

evidence: Bonnabel--Lambert--Bach construct dynamical tangent-space projection algorithms for positive-diagonal plus low-rank Riccati-like approximants, including the matrix differential equation in Section 5. They do not present a closed-form exact-representability boundary for rank-one-forced diagonal Lyapunov Gramians.
Bertsimas--Copenhaver--Mazumder consider general global low-rank factor-analysis optimization and Heywood cases, without a Lyapunov/exponential-kernel rate-pattern theorem or t-cubed distance.
Saunderson et al. treat general diagonal-and-low-rank decompositions and correlation/ellipsoid geometry, not this parameterized family or its short-time distance.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier mathematical problems are broader at the algorithm/optimization level, but a general problem formulation or solver is not a theorem implying the exact class-membership dichotomy and sharp local-distance exponent for this structured input. Standard Cauchy--Schwarz and tetrad algebra are explicitly treated as prior background, not independently claimed.

evidence: The Lyapunov solution is the Gram matrix of exponentials and can be written entrywise as a Cauchy-Laplace kernel, a standard fact. A closed form for its entries alone does not determine which factor-analysis uniqueness variances stay nonnegative.
For the three-rate stationary matrix with rates 1, 2, 3, exact algebra forces the middle uniqueness variance to -1/60; a second, independent construction covers two repeated rate groups.
The leading positive defects are order t^4, while the Gramian entries are order t. Together with a midpoint rank-one upper approximation, this yields the nonzero order t^3 distance.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior factor-analysis and Riccati-projection results establish the model and motivations. Their statements do not logically imply the particular necessary-and-sufficient rate partition or the two-sided cubic distance without the kernel positivity and asymptotic arguments given here. A complete earlier specialized source remains a possible priority threat.

evidence: The one-factor tetrad identity and nonnegative-uniqueness constraints are classical; JMLR 18(2017), Section 1 describes the latent-factor covariance and Heywood negative uniqueness.

The specialized off-diagonal triple defect is strictly positive for all 3-rate diagonal Lyapunov Gramians by an explicit Laplace-kernel 2x2 minor; the full rate-pattern classification includes repeated-rate tetrads.
Bonnabel et al. (2024), Section 3 addresses tangent projections for low-rank plus strictly positive diagonal matrices rather than exact membership of the diagonal Lyapunov solution.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Reexpressing the claim in standard factor-analysis language produces known necessary tetrad and uniqueness inequalities, not a known complete classification of the exponential Gram kernel. The nontrivial missing comparison is supplied by strict Laplace-kernel minors, the rank-group multiplicity cases, and matched cubic bounds. Generic equivalence of the mathematical tasks does not establish that these exact specialized results appeared earlier.

evidence: The 2017 and 2012 full-text general factor-analysis sources do not tabulate the exact diagonal Lyapunov Gramian membership cases; searches of available full texts for Lyapunov/Gramian/Cauchy gave no direct matching theorem.
The 2024 source gives low-rank-plus-diagonal approximation methods and numerical examples rather than a table of representable damping-rate multiplicities.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A static numerical example or a universal factor-analysis decision procedure would not itself supply the all-time classification or the sharp t-cubed separation. No matching fixed table was identified; search absence is treated as risk-aware evidence, not novelty proof.

originality.rationale: Comparative assessment separates classical one-factor tetrads, Heywood phenomena, strict kernel inequalities and low-rank-plus-diagonal numerical projection from the combined all-damping-pattern Gramian classification and sharp cubic separation. The motivating paper and two general-factor-analysis full texts were materially read in their relevant sections and did not contain the combined theorem. Bounded record searches returned no claim that mathematically implies it. value.rationale: One-factor-plus-diagonal positive covariance approximations are motivated by linear-storage filtering and factor analysis. The theorem completely classifies which nontrivial rank-one-driven diagonal Lyapunov covariance trajectories are exactly feasible, and proves that generic positive-definite trajectories lie a quantified positive distance outside the model. The Θ(t^3) order is a matched two-sided benchmark for near-initial-time approximation errors, whereas mere negative uniqueness testing lacks this quantitative and dimensional structural classification. This is a meaningful benchmark for approximability of stable covariance evolution, not a claim about computational speed or general Riccati convergence.
